MUQATIL:73:12-15/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:73:12-15/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:73:12-15/r2.claim: The food that sticks in the throat is zaqqum, and the punishment is painful.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p494#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p494#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p494#4/r1.claim: Food with a ghussa is food that catches in the throat.

TAB-FULL:v23p384#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p384#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p384#2/r1.claim: The food will stick in the eater's throat: it neither goes down nor comes back out.

TAB-FULL:v23p384#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p384#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p384#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says it is a thorn that catches in the throat and can neither enter nor exit.

TAB-FULL:v23p384#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p384#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v23p384#2/r3.claim: Mujāhid identifies the choking food as the tree of Zaqqūm.

TAB-FULL:v23p385/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p385/r1.speaker: حمران بن أعين
TAB-FULL:v23p385/r1.claim: Ḥumrān ibn Aʿyan reports that the Prophet recited the description of shackles, Hell, and choking food, then fainted; al-Ṭabarī gives no grading.

ZAJJAJ:v5p241/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p241/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p241/r5.claim: The choking food is ḍarīʿ, also identified as shibriq, a thorn like ʿawsaj; another verse says they have no food but ḍarīʿ.

NAHHAS:v5p57/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p57/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p57/r8.claim: All the accusative nouns are coordinated; this is Abu Jaʿfar's parsing.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p129/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p129/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p129/r14.claim: Food that catches in the throat is a thorn that neither enters nor comes out.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p129/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p129/r15.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p129/r15.claim: The choking food is the tree of zaqqum.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p372/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p372/r10.speaker: ابن عباس عن عكرمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p372/r10.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas through Ikrima says the thorn catches in the throat and can neither go down nor come out.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p372/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p372/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p372/r7.claim: Food of choking is food that does not go down the throat; a ghussa is whatever causes choking.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p372/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p372/r8.speaker: ابن عباس والمفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p372/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas and the exegetes, along with Mujahid, Muqatil, and Ikrima, identify the choking food as zaqqum.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p372/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p372/r9.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p372/r9.claim: Abu Ishaq says the food is darīʿ, the thorny plant in 88:6, which resembles the osage thorn.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:11-17/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:11-17/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:11-17/r4.claim: Their choking food cannot pass down the throat and consists of foul fluid, thorny plant, and zaqqūm.

JISHUMI:v10p7139#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7139#2/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7139#2/r1.claim: Most readers put the conditional phrase after the object, while Ibn Masud and Atiyya move yawm before in khiftum; Abu al-Sammal uses kasra on the nūn in tattaqūna by annexation, but the agreed form has fatḥa.

JISHUMI:v10p7139#2/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7139#2/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7139#2/r6.claim: Ghuṣṣa is a morsel stuck in the throat and impossible to swallow; a ghuṣṣa in the heart is pain so intense that food and drink cannot pass.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p255/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p255/r12.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p255/r12.claim: God has unbreakable great shackles and choking food, identified as zaqqum and darī‘, followed by painful punishment.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p255/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p255/r13.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p255/r13.claim: Al-Kalbi says the shackles are iron collars; the choking food cannot be swallowed or expelled and is zaqqum and darī‘.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p388#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p388#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p388#2/r6.claim: Mujahid and others identify the choking food as the tree of Zaqqūm.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p388#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p388#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p388#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says the food is fiery thorns lodged in the throat, neither going down nor coming out; all food there can cause choking.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p388#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p388#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p388#2/r8.claim: A report says the Prophet recited this verse and fainted; the author gives no grading.

TABRISI:73:11-14/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:11-14/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:73:11-14/r12.claim: The choking food has thorns that catch in the throat so nothing enters or leaves; alternatives make it rough food or specifically zaqqum and darīʿ.

TABRISI:73:11-14/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:11-14/r13.speaker: حمران بن أعين عن عبد الله بن عمر
TABRISI:73:11-14/r13.claim: A report says the Prophet heard someone recite this verse and fainted.

TABRISI:73:11-14/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:11-14/r4.speaker: عدي بن زيد
TABRISI:73:11-14/r4.claim: His verse about choking without water and a thorny plant shows ghussa as painful choking in the throat.

TABRISI:73:11-14/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:11-14/r6.speaker: طرفة
TABRISI:73:11-14/r6.claim: Tarafa's line describing a heavy cow witnesses wabil as a thick, weighty club; the same root also describes heavy rain and what is burdensome.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p393#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p393#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p393#2/r1.claim: Food that catches in the throat is thorn that neither enters nor comes back out.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p393#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p393#2/r2.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p393#2/r2.claim: The food that catches in the throat is zaqqūm.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p393#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p393#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p393#2/r3.claim: It is ḍarīʿ, a thorny plant.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p393#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p393#2/r4.speaker: الثعلبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p393#2/r4.claim: It may combine zaqqūm, ghislīn, and ḍarīʿ.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:12-14/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:12-14/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:12-14/r12.claim: Ghussa means a morsel, bone, or other thing caught in the throat; the passage also explains its plural, related forms, and the expression for a crowded house.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:12-14/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:12-14/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:73:12-14/r7.claim: The choking food is unswallowable and may be ghislin, zaqqum, or dari‘; Ibn Abbas also says it is a thorn lodged in the throat, neither passing down nor coming out.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:12-14/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:12-14/r8.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:73:12-14/r8.claim: Al-Zajjaj identifies the food as dari‘, citing the statement that they have no food except dari‘; it is a thorn like osage orange.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:12-14/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:12-14/r9.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:73:12-14/r9.claim: Mujahid identifies the food as zaqqum, citing the verse that calls the tree the food of the sinner; Qurtubi says the interpretations converge.

BAYDAWI-FULL:73:10-13/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:10-13/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:10-13/r4.claim: They face choking food such as darīʿ or zaqqūm and another painful punishment whose full nature only God knows; spiritually it is deprivation from seeing God, as attached souls suffer separation and denied holiness.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p291#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p291#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p291#7/r1.claim: The choking food is what sticks in the throat and cannot be swallowed, identified as ḍarīʿ or zaqqūm; its pain reaches the heart.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p291#7/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p291#7/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p291#7/r2.claim: A report says the Prophet recited the verse and fainted.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p291#7/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p291#7/r3.speaker: الحسن
NASAFI-FULL:v4p291#7/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan, while fasting, put aside his meal for three successive evenings when the verse came to mind; Thābit al-Bunānī and others eventually persuaded him to drink a sip of gruel.

QASHANI:73:12-14/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:73:12-14/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:73:12-14/r1.claim: Innerly, religious duties are fetters, effort in seeking is a fire, resisting nature and meeting obligations instead of appetites is choking food, and ascetic struggle is painful torment.

QASHANI:73:12-14/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:73:12-14/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:73:12-14/r3.claim: Alternatively, shackles are painful dispositions and forms, hell is natural fire, choking food is loathed nourishment, and torment comes from those fires and forms.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p309/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p309/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p309/r3.claim: Dhū al-Rummah describes a sleeper wrapped up while his camel crosses a desert, illustrating متزمل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p310/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p310/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p310/r1.claim: The poem's word غصان belongs to the lexical discussion of choking; the commentary distinguishes the plural غصص and forms غاص and غصان.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p316/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p316/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p316/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the choking food is thorns of fire caught in the throat, neither descending nor coming out.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p316/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p316/r6.speaker: مجاهد وغيره
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p316/r6.claim: Mujāhid and others identify the choking food as the tree of Zaqqūm; another view adds the tree of Ḍarīʿ.

SAMIN-DURR:73:13/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:73:13/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:73:13/r1.claim: Ghussa is something lodged in the throat and difficult to swallow; the verb is used with a kasra, with ‘ghasin’ and ‘ghasnan’ as forms for the afflicted person.

SAMIN-DURR:73:13/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:73:13/r2.speaker: الشاعر
SAMIN-DURR:73:13/r2.claim: The anonymous poem compares a throat choked by water with a person whose throat is obstructed by something else, witnessing the choking sense of ghussa.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p256#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p256#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p256#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the food that chokes sticks in the throat and neither enters nor comes out.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p211/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p211/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p211/r5.claim: The choking food may be dariʿ or zaqqum: it catches in the throat and can neither be swallowed nor expelled, contrasting with their refined meals and pursuit of every pleasure.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p211/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p211/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p211/r6.claim: The general painful punishment removes every remaining sweetness from the lives of those who mocked the call to escape sense-bound desire for enduring good works.

DURR-FULL:v8p319/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p319/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p319/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas describes the choking food as thorny, caught in the throat, unable to go in or come out.

DURR-FULL:v8p319/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p319/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p319/r9.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas identifies the choking food as the tree of Zaqqum; Mujahid gives the same view.

BURSEVI:v10p164#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p164#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p164#2/r10.claim: The damned receive this food because they consumed God’s blessings while disbelieving in them; it opposes the pleasant food of Paradise.

BURSEVI:v10p164#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p164#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p164#2/r11.claim: The indefinite phrase “painful punishment” encompasses further kinds of torment whose measure and true nature cannot be grasped.

BURSEVI:v10p164#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p164#2/r12.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v10p164#2/r12.claim: A report says the Prophet collapsed unconscious when this verse was revealed.

BURSEVI:v10p164#2/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p164#2/r13.speaker: الحسن البصري
BURSEVI:v10p164#2/r13.claim: Hasan al-Basri repeatedly put away food while fasting after encountering this verse; visitors eventually persuaded him to drink a little sawīq.

BURSEVI:v10p164#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p164#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p164#2/r9.claim: The choking food sticks in the throat and can neither be swallowed nor expelled; the worldly plants called darīʿ and zaqqum are poisonous and repulsive, so their hellish forms are worse still.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p107#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p107#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p107#4/r1.claim: The choking food catches in the throat and is difficult to swallow, like dariʿ or zaqqum; Ibn Abbas describes fiery thorns that neither rise nor descend.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p107#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p107#4/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p107#4/r2.claim: The painful punishment is beyond measurement or knowledge except God's; its indefinite wording signals something grave.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p107#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p107#4/r3.speaker: أبو حرب بن الأسود
ALUSI-FULL:v29p107#4/r3.claim: A report through Abu Harb says the Prophet heard a man recite the passage about restraints and fainted; another version says the Prophet himself recited until أليما and fainted.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p107#4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p107#4/r4.speaker: خالد بن حسان
ALUSI-FULL:v29p107#4/r4.claim: Khalid ibn Hassan relates that al-Hasan refused food after hearing the verse for three nights, then drank a little gruel after visitors urged him.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p107#4/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p107#4/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p107#4/r5.claim: If sound, the report excuses Sufis who faint when hearing verses and qualifies Aisha's criticism, unless she objected only to deliberate swooning or to a different kind of صعق.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p107#4/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p107#4/r6.speaker: الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v29p107#4/r6.claim: Al-Razi reads four punishments spiritually: bodily attachments bind the soul, frustrated desire burns it, deprivation chokes it, and exclusion from divine disclosure is painful; he retains both bodily and spiritual senses.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p107#4/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p107#4/r7.speaker: الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v29p107#4/r7.claim: Al-Razi says the indefinite عذابا marks a punishment more intense and complete than those preceding it.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p107#4/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p107#4/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p107#4/r8.claim: The author objects that applying both literal and figurative meanings together lacks a contextual indicator and notes that much Sufi allusive interpretation faces this issue.

ELMALILI:73:2-19#3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:2-19#3/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:2-19#3/r11.claim: The choking food is identified with things such as zaqqūm, ghislīn, and darīʿ: it sticks in the throat and can neither be swallowed nor brought back up, alongside unbearable pain.

ELMALILI:73:2-19#3/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:2-19#3/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:2-19#3/r12.claim: The Prophet is reported to have cried out when reciting this verse.

ELMALILI:73:2-19#3/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:2-19#3/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:2-19#3/r13.claim: Hasan al-Baṣrī repeatedly set aside his ifṭār after recalling the choking-food verse, until Sābit al-Bunānī, Yazīd al-Ḍabbī, and Yaḥyā al-Bakkā persuaded him to drink barley-water.

TABATABAI:73:1-19#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:1-19#2/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
TABATABAI:73:1-19#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that the Prophet heard a reciter say food of choking and swooned.

TABATABAI:73:13-17/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:13-17/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:13-17/r1.claim: Ghussa is food stuck in the throat that cannot be swallowed; the term can also describe a persistent knot or sting in the heart.

TABATABAI:73:13-17/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:13-17/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:13-17/r2.claim: The verses describe punishments of the afterlife replacing worldly blessings, as requital for ingratitude toward God's gifts.

ASAD-NOTES:73:11#n7/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:73:11#n7/r1.speaker: Razi
ASAD-NOTES:73:11#n7/r1.claim: Razi reads all four torments as spiritual consequences: attachment to bodily pleasures shackles the soul and blocks purity, frustration burns, deprivation chokes, and separation from God's light and the blessed is grievous.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p10/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p10/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p10/r1.claim: He thought reaching Sūrah Tawbah would suffice to demonstrate the truth and value of his late mentor’s interpretive principles.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p10/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p10/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p10/r2.claim: After recovery and relocation to a village with few amenities, he resolved to write Tadabbur-i Qur’an as gratitude for renewed strength.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p10/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p10/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p10/r3.claim: He composed many sūrah commentaries outdoors under trees amid heat, birds, hornets, and flies, absorbed in explaining difficult verses.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p10/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p10/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p10/r4.claim: He regarded writing as his duty, while publication and sales were not his responsibility.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p10/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p10/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p10/r5.claim: His household lived on land inherited by his wife, and he trusted God to provide for him in old age.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p11/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p11/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p11/r1.claim: He reports that scholars and educated readers across regions value the tafsir’s method, which is being used for Qur’anic teaching and studied in research.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p11/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p11/r2.speaker: Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p11/r2.claim: His mentor urged complete research and deliberation before writing or speaking, since strong reasoning endures and weak arguments soon disappear.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p11/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p11/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p11/r3.claim: The tafsir does not claim to encompass Qur’anic knowledge; the Qur’an is inexhaustible, and the work only opens a way to deliberate on it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p12/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p12/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p12/r1.claim: Applying the tafsir’s principles can reveal Qur’anic wisdom, help judge disputes across disciplines, and loosen sectarian blind following; later scholars must continue the work.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p12/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p12/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p12/r2.claim: Readers should assess what is said rather than who said it, because truth belongs to everyone and failing to recognize it harms the rejecter.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p13/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p13/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p13/r1.claim: On finishing the tafsir, he prayed that God accept his service to the Qur’an and make it a means of salvation, asking readers to say amen.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p13/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p13/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p13/r2.claim: He credits Ghulām Ṣamdānī with devoted, skillful copying of the manuscripts, more help than even his sons.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p13/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p13/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p13/r3.claim: ‘Abdullāh Ghulām Aḥmad helped copy the manuscript and used his intelligence to resolve exegetical problems.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p13/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p13/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p13/r4.claim: Khalīd Mas‘ūd and Javed Aḥmad helped locate references for citations.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p13/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p13/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p13/r5.claim: Majid Khāwar took charge of publication under a schedule and successfully completed it as promised.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p13/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p13/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p13/r6.claim: He thanks his collaborators and prays that God grant them service that brings success in this life and the next.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p25/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p25/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p25/r4.claim: Those who fail to meet the obligation of their abundant food and resources will face food lodged in their throats and painful punishment.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p9/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p9/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p9/r1.claim: The Qur’an is a God-given standard for distinguishing good from evil; Muslims need its true knowledge and practice, not recitation merely for reward or commercial use.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p9/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p9/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p9/r2.claim: True Qur’anic knowledge reforms the community through practice, following the way its earliest generations were reformed.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p9/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p9/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p9/r3.claim: He undertook the tafsir as an obligation, despite seeing it as a hazardous undertaking whose completion was not assured.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p9/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p9/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p9/r4.claim: When severe illness stopped his mental work in 1971–72, he accepted that the tafsir might remain unfinished as God willed.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:11/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:11/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:11/r4.claim: The passage also mentions a painful punishment whose nature is not specified.

STUDYQURAN:73:13/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:73:13/r1.speaker: JJ
STUDYQURAN:73:13/r1.claim: Choking food may include Zaqqūm, a vile thorn, inedible filth, and fiery thorns that cannot be vomited or swallowed; alternatively, these may collectively describe the food.
